[i]Erene:2000 Expansion Roleplay[/i]]

[b][December 7th, 1980][/b]

It was a sweltering hot summer day in Luscária, the Sun was bearing down causing the streets to smoke. Children could be seen running through the streets chasing after one another, the streets were bustling with life, the honking of cars, the loud voices of passerbys. But far away from all the liveliness there was a large conference room, despite being well lit there was a heavy darkness enshrouding the place, a suffocating stale air and the thick stench of a cigar all backdropped by the constant ticking of a clock. In the room was Caudillo Luis Garcia Rodriguez, State Marshal Pablo Escobar, Minister of State Security Juan Bautista Topete, and Minister of Finance Raúl Chibás. The four men were gathered around a couple maps, there was a detailed map of Luscária alongside the maps of Southwest Vespurias and a global map of Erene, on the maps one could spot many circled areas, potential points of interest and small notes written besides them detailing an estimated value of each area and the potential dangers to be found there.

Today was not like any other day, Caudillo Luis G. Rodriguez had been making plans for years now, all leading up to this moment. It was February 13th, 1967 when his predecessor launched El Sendero de las Lágrimas, it was a special operation with the purpose of reclaiming rightful Luscárian land and returning order to the surrounding areas. During El Sendero de las Lágrimas the SVA (States Vanguard Army) was tasked with securing the borders of Luscária, reclaiming the land to the East, ensuring the compliance of any native tribes found in the area, and the elimination of any destabilizing factors in the surrounding area. For 2 years 1 month and 8 days the SVA would continue its relentless march eastward, carefully relocating countless natives, and crushing the budding nations of the war lords and illegal breakaways who dared to occupy Luscárian land. March 21st, 1969 on this day El Sendero de las Lágrimas would come to an end as a massive success, expanding the Luscárian borders by 428,000 km^2 and setting the foundation for further expansion. Another period of rapid development and stabilization would be brought about and would continue until today, Caudillo Rodriguez had long been making plans to commence an operation of even larger scale than El Sendero de las Lágrimas and finally after years of development the Luscárian war machine was ready to begin operations once more.

Minister Chibás began, [i]Luscária has managed to fully digest its previous gains. The area has been stabilized and rendered productive. Infrastructure output in the eastern zones exceeds projections. Agricultural yields have stabilized. Resource extraction has reached sustainable efficiency.[/i]

He adjusted his glasses and a stack of documents on the table.

[i]Weve achieved a great success in incorporating the eastern zone into Luscária, but there remains a great inefficiency that continues to drag Luscária down.[/i]

Raúl gestured toward the northern frontier on the map.

[i]Our northern border is inefficient. Poorly defined. It is populated by semi-autonomous communities that contribute little to the State, but who continue to demand from us. As of this moment they exist in a state of tolerated disorder, disorder that continues to drain our resources.[/i]

Caudillo Rodriguez said nothing, he merely nodded once.

Minister Topete picked up where Chibás left off, [i]That independence they so seem to value is nothing more than a facade. For far too long weve allowed them to delude themselves into thinking they were an actual state, delusions like these will only serve to undermine the unity of Luscária. It is about time Luscária reclaimed its rightful land, about time we reminded them of their place.[/i]

State Marshal Escobar took a large puff of his cigar stabbing a knife into the circled area to the north of Luscária.

[i]Their spirits have long been broken, they rightfully fear the State. They are hardly worth mentioning before what we have planned. The Northern Administrative Region is a Luscárian territory in everything but name at this point. The real focus of the SVA is the land to the east of Luscária. Those lands remain defiant, ignorant of the glory of the Paramount State.[/i]

Pablo Escobar straightened his back and stared straight at the Caudillo, [i]The Northern Administrative Region will be brought under control before the year ends. Then I will lead the SVA to march through the eastern wastes to spread the light of Luscária to them."[/i]

Luis stared at the impaled map for a second, glancing at the small detailed red paths drawn, before staring at Pablo Escobar. In a dull voice lacking any inflection he quietly told him, [i]Proceed, this time without waste.[/i]

[b][December 8th, 1980][/b]

The orders were issued without ceremony.

At 06:00 hours, directives bearing the seal of the Caudillo were transmitted simultaneously to provincial governors, SVA High Command, and the Ministry of State Security. Officially these decrees were framed as administrative restructuring measures, an effort to improve border security, suppress smuggling and restore public order.

La Marcha del Estado had begun.

Within days the Northern Administrative Zones of Luscária underwent a quiet transformation. State Security detachments moved first, establishing forward offices in key towns under the pretext of census verification and infrastructure inspection. Communications hubs were temporarily nationalized, local radio stations placed under supervisory authority, and travel permits introduced along major transit routes. What resistance existed was disorganized, many still believed this to be another transient show of force.

They would soon realize how wrong this belief was as SVA logistics columns followed close behind. Armored transports rolled northward along newly reinforced highways, their passage announced by the grinding of tracks and the rumble of engines that echoed throughout the area. Field depots were erected with mechanical precision. Fuel reserves, ammunition stockpiles, and ration stores appeared almost overnight, camouflaged beneath tarpaulins and netting.

State Marshal Escobar personally oversaw the forward deployment.

[i]The objective is compression,[/i] he instructed his officers. [i]Isolate, surround, then absorb. No spectacular engagements. No martyrdom. We deny them the illusion of resistance.[/i]

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Finance initiated a parallel offensive.

Subsidies to local governments were suspended pending compliance reviews. Banking access was restricted, tax arrears abruptly enforced, and trade licenses invalidated without explanation. Markets faltered within days. Merchants found their supply lines severed, and local authorities, long reliant on state tolerance, scrambled to reassure populations they no longer controlled.

Minister Chibás projections were clear: economic paralysis would succeed where force alone might fail.

Behind the scenes, the Ministry of State Security worked relentlessly under the guidance of Minister Topete.

Lists were compiled; community leaders, militia organizers, religious figures, and foreign intermediaries. Informants were embedded, old rivalries reignited, quiet arrests conducted under the cover of routine security sweeps. Those taken rarely returned, and when they did, they spoke little.

By the third week of December, the illusion of autonomy had begun to fracture. Checkpoints dotted the northern roads. Flags of the State were raised over municipal buildings for the duration of the restructuring process. Local councils were informed that provisional administrators would soon be appointed to assist with governance.

The message was unmistakable.

On the evening of December 18th, Caudillo Luis G. Rodriguez received the first consolidated report.

Northern resistance remained fragmented. No unified command had emerged. External interference was minimal. The population, though uneasy, was compliant.

Caudillo Rodriguez closed the file and stared out across the capital from his office window, watching the sun sink into the haze. [i]This is only the opening phase,[/i] he said quietly to no one in particular.

Beyond the northern horizon, the State was already in motion.

[b][July 23rd, 1984][/b]

The Southern islands had been securely held for a couple weeks at this point, it seemed that soon La Marcha del Estado would come to an end as a great success. But today High Command had received some special information, information regarding the Callistan territories. For a long time now Callista had us fooled that they held an iron grip over the South Coast of Southwest Vespurias, but investigations performed by agents in the area have found that that is not quite true. There exists an area which has pushed back against the Callistans and continuously denied their attempts to conquer them; this area was instead ruled by anthropomorphic Jaguar people.

[i]Should we prepare our forces to invade the area?[/i] asked State Marshal Escobar.

[i]No not yet. Have them ready for immediate transport, but do not deploy. I know of a much better way to deal with that little zoo,[/i] the Caudillo responded, a sharp light appearing in his eyes as he turned to address Minister Topete. [i]Initiate an external resolution. Black-Seal authorization.[/i]

Topete inclined his head, [i]A broker will be dispatched.[/i]

[i]Ensure deniability,[/i] Luis added. [i]This is an opportunity the State cannot miss.[/i]

[b][July 31st, 1984][/b]

Two men could be seen on the beach, one of them was fully engulfed within a red and gold robe, while the other man was visibly bruised and chained. [i]Let us see, according to the book once weve reached the target area the procedure can begin,[/i] muttered the robed man, Jorge Tomaz. [i]A ring of blood then we have to set a person of tainted belief on fire and finally I have to recite the prepared incantation. Well then, that seems simple enough, I see no reason to keep the Caudillo waiting any longer than necessary.[/i]

He pulled out a jug of blood from within his robes, dipped his fingers in the blood and began to draw an intricate portal to another dimension on the sand. By the time the blood in the jug had run out Jorge had managed to finish the portal. He then grabbed the bruised man and threw him into the circle, he had been drugged before Jorge had even begun to ensure his compliance, so he just stood there staring blankly into the sky as Jorge doused him in gasoline before throwing a lit match on him. The blood curdling screams of the man could be heard crying out throughout the entire area, [i]Hmm, at least in your final moments you serve some kind of use. Consider yourself lucky, youve been granted the honor of becoming a useful asset.[/i] Jorge dully remarked before opening the old weathered book he held and beginning to recite the incantation.

[i]Esteemed Representative of Interdimensional Markets,
Broker of Inter-Hyperversal Exchange,
We submit refuse to be recycled.

A feral population infests land designated for greater purpose.
They lack sovereignty.
They lack worth.
They do not qualify to be trampled beneath our boots.

These abominations are not enemies.
They are filth.

We decline to expend soldiers on these animals.
We decline to dignify them with battle.
We decline to acknowledge their extinction as loss.

Dispose of them.

Discard their superfluous physical forms.
Render them into their basic materials.
Reform them as you see fit.
Let their bodies serve a purpose they never could.

To rid the world of these pests,
Is all we require.

To process them into value,
Is what we offer in return.

If these terms are acceptable,
If the assets please You,
Then arrive and commence liquidation.[/i]

As Jorge finished speaking a heavy silence descended upon the place, even the screams of the prisoner had gone mute, the world changed to black and white, all color drained of it. The flames on the prisoner were instantly extinguished, but his body began to split open as if one were opening a book. But there was no blood, no organs, his body split to reveal a rift to endless abyss, a darkness that seemed to actively be devouring all the surrounding light. From the end of the Abyss a hand could be seen reaching out, stretching for an infinite length until it grabbed the edge of the Abyss then another hand reached out grabbing the other side of the Abyss. Both hands proceeded to pull against the rift tearing it open, meanwhile a primordial scream of pain could be heard resounding from the very world itself. Finally once the rift spread all the way to the sky the being began to walk out.

[i]*Tap* *tap* *tap*[/i]

Footsteps resounded through the area as a man in a black suit with a green slime for a head gradually walked out of the Abyss. [i]Fellas, hypothetical question,[/i] the figure said casually, its voice layered, as if several speakers were slightly out of sync with one another. [i]If a product is defective at the manufacturing stage, do you scrap it immediately, or do you find a way to extract remaining value first?[/i]

The things head shifted, viscous green matter rolling and reshaping itself as if attempting to approximate facial expressions without fully understanding them. Where eyes should have been, shapes formed briefly, then dissolved. Its attention slowly turned toward Jorge Tomaz.

[i]Hmm, youre not the customer. Youre just the broker,[/i] it continued, straightening its suit and brushing ash from its sleeve. [i]Regardless, its a pleasure to finally meet you in person. I am the Salesman.[/i]

The abyss behind it sealed itself shut with a sound like wet fabric tearing, leaving the beach unnaturally pristine. The sand no longer shifted beneath the wind. The ocean beyond had gone still, frozen as if painted.

Jorge bowed slightly to the Salesman before addressing it, [i]Your arrival has proven to be most timely, I hope you a[/i]

[i]Yes, yes. I know why youve summoned me here,[/i] the Salesman said, cutting off Jorge. [i]You wish to buy my wares, no? I know just the right thing for you, you should buy the 'Renault Twingo'. Unlike any car youve seen before it comes equipped with the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense system and an AN/TPY-2 transportable radar giving you onboard missile interception capabilities to beat the 'Albin Gambit Nuclear Powered Ballistic Missile Submarine Variation' along with any other gambit that utilizes a missile to checkmate you. In fact if you buy now Ill even throw in a head that never stops screaming, free of charge.[/i]

[i]*Clap*[/i]

As soon as he finished speaking the Salesman clapped his hand together and next to him appeared a massive car and a decapitated screaming head in the passenger seat.

Jorge was dumbfounded at the series of events taking place. He was sure that there had been no mistake in the summoning, and yet the Salesman didnt quite seem to be what he expected, [i]There must be a mistake. I clearly told you what I wanted and what you would get. What is the meaning of this? Do you not intend to follow the contract weve made?[/i]

The Salesman looked at Jorge and answered him swiftly. 

[i]First of all, mortal, never doubt the integrity of a salesman, especially when that salesman is me. Be thankful that unlike others I hold no grudge against your ignorant disrespect, for I have long been enlightened in what truly matters, profit. Now then, I can see that you are ungrateful for the wares I bring with me, and I no longer wish to waste my time on you. I will harvest my assets and in turn leave this land to you, but it seems to me that this exchange benefits you more than it does I. Still, it has been ages since one of you mortals has summoned me to this realm so Ill cut you a special deal. I will cleanse this land of any who may dare to defy you if you give me 40 years of your lifespan and an arm.[/i]

Jorge did not like the way things were developing, it seemed that the original plan could no longer be followed to the letter. However when he wondered what would happen to him if the deal failed and what the Caudillo would do to him, Jorge realized that he hardly had a choice in this matter. He wasnt in any position to negotiate, at best he was the broker for the Caudillo. From the very beginning he was no different from the prisoner, both had been sent to serve as the sacrifices for the advancement of the Caudillos plans. So he reluctantly agreed and reached out to the Salesman with his right hand.

[i]*Riiiiip*[/i]

The Salesman shook Jorges hand, a blue flame engulfing them, before it ripped his arm off.

When the blue flame faded away Jorge could be seen kneeling on the ground, he had visibly aged and he was excessively bleeding from where his right arm once used to be. Jorge was gasping trying to fight back against the pain, his veins bulging out and his left arm clamped onto his bloody stump. [i]Its certainly been a pleasure doing business with you. Now, time to harvest my little broken toys,[/i] the Salesman said before vanishing into thin air.

[b][August 2nd, 1984][/b]

The first SVA landing craft made landfall at dawn.

The ramps lowered onto untouched sand. No resistance greeted them. No scouts. No fortifications. No signs of flight or last stands. The air was still in a way that unsettled even veteran troops, heavy and oppressive, as if the world itself had come to a stop.

Captain Esteban Rojas was the first to step onto the beach, his boots leaving no footprints. He paused, crouched down and pressed a gloved hand into the sand. It did not shift. It did not cling. It felt compacted, as if it had already been processed beforehand. Behind him, infantry squads fanned outward in practiced formation, rifles raised, optics sweeping the treeline that never came.

There were no trees.

Inland stretched a vast emptiness. Hills flattened into shallow gradients. Rivers reduced to dry channels etched into the ground like diagrams rather than geography. Structures did exist but not dwellings, not settlements, not anything that could reasonably house life.

Billboards stood alone at irregular intervals. Perfectly upright, their metal supports gleamed faintly in the morning light, unmarred by rust or decay. Each displaying the same figure; a man in a pristine black suit, one hand raised mid-gesture, the other presenting a product. His head was a translucent green slime, seeming to be smiling.

Some billboards advertised cars, others furniture or household appliances. One of them even depicted a neatly stacked pile of bricks, labeled: ENERGY BARS,  LOCALLY SOURCED.

There were no roads leading to the billboards. No paths, no tracks, these billboards seemed to serve no purpose with no audience to view them. No audience except the SVA, but did that mean that someone or something knew they would come? And even if that were the case why would they choose to set up advertisement billboards?

Ignoring the surreal atmosphere the recon teams pushed deeper inland. What little wildlife the reports had mentioned was completely absent. In its place all that remained was a suffocating silence

By midday, the conclusion was unavoidable.

There had once been a civilization here. Now? There was none.

At 14:30 hours, Captain Rojas filed his report.

[i]Area secure,[/i] he stated flatly. [i]No hostile presence, no civilians. No identifiable governing structures. The land appears processed.[/i] He hesitated before adding, [i]Requesting clarification on follow-up objectives.[/i]

High Commands response came within minutes.

[i]Begin formal annexation procedures. Establish forward bases. Inventory terrain and extractive potential. The matter of prior inhabitants is considered resolved,[/i] and with that the transmission ended.

As the States flag was raised over land that had never known it, the billboards continued to stand in silence, their smiling salesman eternally mid-pitch, offering products to no one at all.

[b][August 15th, 1984][/b]

A slouching figure wrapped in red and gold robes approached the Palacio del Estado just before dawn.

He moved slowly, unevenly, as if each step required negotiation with his own body. The robe hung loose on him, its fabric dragging across the stone as though it had once belonged to someone larger, someone healthier. Dark stains crusted the hem, old and new layered together.

State Security halted him at the outer checkpoint. [i]Halt! Identify yourself and state your purpose,[/i] the officers demanded as they pointed their guns at the robed figure.

The figure paused, unmoving for several seconds. It seemed he might not respond at all. Then, with a trembling hand, he reached beneath the robe and produced a metal emblem bearing the seal of the Caudillo. His grip faltered, and one of the officers caught it before it struck the ground.

[i]I am Jorge Tomaz,[/i] he said at last. His voice was dry, frayed thin by exhaustion. [i]I am here to report on the completion of a Black-Seal operation.[/i]

The officers exchanged a glance.
The seal was authentic. That was enough.

They escorted him inside. Under the palace lights, what remained of Jorge was impossible to ignore.

His skin sagged loosely against bone, stretched thin and translucent. His hair had turned almost entirely white. Where his right arm had once been, there was only a blackened stump wrapped in layers of filthy bandage, the fabric stiff with dried blood and yellow pus. The wound had not been properly treated, infection had already set in. His entire body emitted an aura of decay and rot, as if what walked through the palace halls wasnt human, but some rotting corpse.

But the condition of Jorge did not slow their pace.

Jorge stumbled more than once as they crossed the marble floors, leaving faint, irregular smears behind him.

No one commented. No one offered assistance beyond ensuring he continued to walk.

Caudillo Luis G. Rodriguez did not rise when Jorge was brought before him.

Luis sat behind his desk, hands folded, posture immaculate. Minister Topete stood to his right, expression unreadable. Surgeon General Alejandro Ramirez waited near the doorway, already observing Jorge with professional detachment, eyes tracking tremors, discoloration, pupil dilation.

Jorge tried to kneel, but his legs failed him. One of the officers forced him upright again.

[i]Report,[/i] the Caudillo said calmly.

Jorge swallowed. His throat worked for several seconds before sound finally emerged. [i]It it is done,[/i] he rasped. [i]The territory has been cleansed. No resistance remains. The the entity upheld its end of the agreement.[/i]

Luis studied him for a long moment. His gaze lingered not on the missing arm, nor the ruined flesh, but on Jorges eyes.

[i]Efficient,[/i] the Caudillo said at last. [i]You have served the State well.[/i]

Jorge exhaled shakily, something between relief and collapse.

Luis turned his head slightly, addressing Topete without raising his voice. [i]Send him to the Ministry of Health,[/i] he said. [i]The Surgeon General will oversee his examination. Full documentation. Longitudinal study. Whatever can still be learned from him will belong to Luscária.[/i]

Juan Topete nodded once before walking towards Jorge. Surgeon General Ramirez took the lead as he began to walk back to the Ministry of Health.

Jorges eyes widened in dawning understanding. His mouth opened as if to speak, but no words came. Whatever protest might have existed died somewhere between thought and breath.

As he was led away, leaving faint dark stains on the polished floor, Luis returned his attention to the map spread across his desk.

Another territory marked complete.
Another inefficiency removed.

La Marcha del Estado was nearing its conclusion and the State had once again proven that no obstacle, no matter how unusual, could stand in the way of its expansion.

The clock continued to tick.
[/spoiler]
